name: NE5534 / NE5534A / SA5534 / SE5534 (incl. NJM5534) - single low-noise decompensated bipolar
tagline: Signetics' 1979 low-noise decompensated single and the 5532's forerunner: about 3.5 nV/rtHz, 10 MHz and 600-ohm drive. A staple of consoles, CD/DAC stages and MM/mic preamps.
technology: Bipolar single op amp, decompensated: internally compensated for gains of about 3 or more. For unity or low gain, an external capacitor goes between COMP and COMP/BAL (pins 5 and 8). The TI datasheet headline figures of 13 V/us and 10 MHz UGBW were confirmed by web search. onsemi NE5534/D carries the Signetics-derived wording ('Compared to other operational amplifiers such as TL083...'). Dave Jones (EEVblog 1752) notes that the TI NE5532 and NE5534 'haven't always been exactly the same design'.

reputation.summary: The single-channel, decompensated forerunner of the NE5532. It is lower in noise than the 5532 and drives 600-ohm loads. Douglas Self covers it alongside the 5532 in his books, and it is widely used in MM phono, mic and line stages of consoles, CD players, DAC filter stages and ADC drivers (the AKM AK5383 reference circuit uses NJM5534). Dave Jones (EEVblog) treats it as a low-noise audio default. diyAudio posters (not re-verified) say it sounds good when correctly compensated, and it is a common baseline that upgrades such as the OPA627 are compared against. Soomal (China) calls the TI NE5534 fitted in the Creative AE-9 clearly lower grade than the LM49710 it replaced. It also notes Matrix using the 'old-flavour' NE5534 in the HPA-2 Classic low-pass filter. In Japan, vintage Signetics/Philips NOS parts have a following, and bloggers rank them above TI and JRC versions (anecdotal).
sonic_descriptors: neutral / clean when properly compensated (diyAudio, anecdotal)
softer and less 'hard' than AD797/OPA1611, but less dynamic and resolving (Soomal, AE-9 op-amp roll)
vintage Signetics/Philips NOS described as an upgrade over TI/JRC (Japanese blogs, anecdotal)
typical_uses: CD-player / DAC I/V and low-pass filter stages (e.g. Matrix M-Stage HPA-2 Classic LPF)
ADC input drivers (AKM AK5383 reference circuit uses NJM5534)
socketed op-amp positions in sound cards (Creative AE-9 ships TI NE5534)
caveats: Decompensated: in a unity-gain or low-gain socket it needs the external COMP to COMP/BAL capacitor. Dropping it into a unity-gain buffer position can oscillate.
Second-source parts (Signetics/Philips, TI, onsemi, JRC) are separate vendor products. Differences in compensation margin are community reports only, so verify stability when swapping brands.
The TI NE5532 and NE5534 are not guaranteed identical designs (EEVblog 1752). Don't assume 5532 behaviour carries over to the 5534, or the reverse.
TI NE5534AD (SOIC tube) is reported EOL; TI points to NE5534ADRG4. Distributors have at times shown NE5534 variants as obsolete although TI lists them as active.

TI's NE5532 redesign (PCN20231114002.1: abs-max supply +/-22 V to +/-18 V, ESD 2 kV to 1 kV) does NOT apply to the NE5534 as of Sep 2026. SLOS070D (Nov 2014) is still current. Re-check for any SLOS070E or NE5534 PCN.
JRC NJM5534D/M are obsolete; the current JRC part is NJM5534DD.

silicon_changes.identification: Claimed: older parts carry pad-printed (tampo) Signetics marking and later parts are laser-marked Philips. Not vendor-documented.
silicon_changes.summary: Japanese blogs (radiokits.jp, takinx.dcnblog.jp) claim the Signetics masters were lost in the 2000 Philips Albuquerque fab fire and that Philips redrew the layout. Signetics did have Albuquerque fabs (FAB22/FAB23), but no source links a fire to an NE5534 redesign. A conflicting community claim says a fire at NXP's Caen, France fab ended NXP's 553x production. No vendor PCN or datasheet supports either claim.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Anecdotal only: Japanese listeners prefer older pad-printed Signetics new-old-stock parts. No measurements found.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low - no documented datasheet change; unverified folklore.
silicon_changes.verification: Not re-searched (folklore kind). The earlier pass found Signetics Albuquerque fabs but no document linking a fire to an NE5534 redesign.

silicon_changes.vendor: Multiple second sources (Signetics/Philips vs TI vs onsemi vs JRC NJM5534)
silicon_changes.identification: Manufacturer logo and prefix on the package (Signetics/Philips 'N' suffix, TI logo, ON logo, JRC 'NJM').
silicon_changes.summary: Each vendor sells its own part under the same generic number; GroupDIY posters say each company uses its own production mask. GroupDIY and Head-Fi threads and Japanese blogs report behavioural and sonic differences. Separate vendor-specific SPICE models exist (NJM5534, NE5534ON, NE5534PH, NE5534TI). Datasheet-level deltas between vendors were not retrieved.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Community reports rank Signetics/Philips above TI/JRC (anecdotal). Stability margins in low-gain positions may differ.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium - check stability and compensation when swapping brands in unity-gain or low-gain sockets.
silicon_changes.verification: Not re-searched (second-source kind). Kept as reported.

counterfeit_notes: Marketplaces sell 'Signetics / former Philips NE5534N' NOS (e.g. eBay listings); remarked fakes are reported in discovery notes but not independently verified. Japanese blogs say NOS NE5534 sells above NE5532, which would make relabelling attractive (anecdotal). Genuine OEM house-numbered Signetics NE5534s also exist (HP custom part numbers, per EEVblog), so an odd marking is not proof of a fake. Precautions: be sceptical of large 'NOS Signetics' lots, check that the marking style and date code fit the claimed era, and buy current production (TI NE5534P/NE5534AP/ADRG4, onsemi, NJM5534DD) from authorised distributors. Bench-check noise and stability: a decompensated part at unity gain without the cap may oscillate, which can mask other differences.

revision_chain_notes:
TI SLOS070 (NE5534/NE5534A/SE5534/SE5534A, later SA5534/SA5534A). Known chain: the original edition (JULY 1979 - REVISED SEPTEMBER 1990; the date is now re-confirmed by a search summary; SE-grade title), then B (FEB 2004), C (SEP 2004), and D (NOV 2014, still current). Missing: SLOS070A was not found. One search summary claimed 'SLOS070A' is the NE5534/SA5534 document number, but no copy showed an SLOS070A header, so it is not recorded. Also missing: the change log for B and whether A (c.1990s-2003) exists. Pre-1990 TI editions, if any, were not found.

Philips Semiconductors (Signetics successor) product specifications. Two found, oldest to newest. (1) NE5533/5533A/5534/5534A 'Dual and single low noise op amp', 1994 Aug 31 (alldatasheet 17973, 8 pp; also 17975, datasheet4u 454296, chipfind, pcbfacile 'Linear Products'). (2) NE/SA/SE5534/5534A 'Single low noise operational amplifier', 2001 Aug 03, which supersedes 1994 Aug 31 (esr.co.uk copy likely; datasheetcatalog SE5534). Missing: any pre-1994 Philips edition, the Signetics-branded originals (1979-1990s data-book sheets; datasheetarchive has a 'NE5534 Signetics' index, contents not seen), and the exact legacy semiconductors.philips.com/acrobat URL (only the datasheet.live mirror path shows the host). No NXP-era edition after 2001 was found.

onsemi/ON Semiconductor NE5534/D. Found: Rev. 3 (July 2012, mouser NE5534-D-99992.pdf) and Rev. 4 (December 2024, current onsemi.com). Missing: Rev. 0-2 (ON Semiconductor pub/Collateral era, probably 2000s); seeds are http://www.onsemi.com/pub/Collateral/NE5534-D.PDF and the PowerSolutions product page.

JRC/NJR/Nisshinbo NJM5534. No 'Ver.' date was shown in any summary. Copies were found (alldatasheet 7454/7455 older NJM5534/NJM5534D; 515327 NJM5534DD 6 pp; datasheet4u 455113; datasheetq), plus a Scribd 'Discontinued NJM5534 Notice' (NJM5534-2-22-11). All Ver. dates are still missing.

STMicroelectronics. A dedicated search found no ST NE5534 datasheet; it remains unconfirmed whether ST ever second-sourced the single NE5534.

The archive seeds focus.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ne5534.pdf and sa5534.pdf follow TI's historic URL pattern and were not seen in results. http://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ne5534.pdf appeared in a summary.
